title: Spiced Minced Beef Keema with Soft Rolls
summary: A fragrant Indian keema of minced beef cooked down with browned onion, ginger, garlic, warm spices, tomato and yoghurt until thick and rich. Served with warm soft rolls and a squeeze of lime.
equipment: large saucepan or deep frying pan (24-28 cm) with lid

ingredients.item: large red onion, halved and thinly sliced
fine sea salt or table salt
Kashmiri chilli powder (or 1.5 tsp sweet paprika plus a pinch of cayenne)

steps.title: Fry the whole spices
steps.text: Heat the oil in the saucepan over medium heat, add the peppercorns, cardamom and cinnamon and stir for 30 seconds until fragrant. Frying whole spices releases their aromatic oils into the fat, which then flavours the whole dish.

steps.title: Brown the onion
steps.text: Add the onion and cook for 8-10 minutes, stirring, until well browned. Deeply coloured onion brings sweetness and a savoury depth to the sauce.

steps.title: Cook the mince dry
steps.text: Stir in the garlic and ginger for 30 seconds, then add the mince and salt. Turn the heat up to medium-high and cook for 8-12 minutes, breaking the meat into very small pieces with the spoon, until the liquid has gone, the meat sizzles and the base of the pan looks dry and browned. Driving off the moisture lets the meat fry and brown instead of stewing.

steps.title: Add ground spices
steps.text: Add the coriander, chilli powder, turmeric and cumin and stir for 1 minute. Cooking the ground spices briefly in the fat takes away any raw, dusty taste.

steps.title: Simmer with tomato
steps.text: Add the tomatoes, yoghurt and green chilli and stir until simmering. Cover and cook over low heat for 15-20 minutes, stirring now and then, until the tomatoes have broken down and a spoon dragged across the pan leaves a clear trail. Check that a thermometer in the keema reads at least 71 °C.

steps.title: Finish with herbs
steps.text: Remove the cinnamon stick and cardamom pods if you like. Stir in most of the coriander, then sprinkle with the garam masala and the remaining coriander; added at the end, the garam masala keeps its fresh, warm aroma.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Serve the keema hot with the warm rolls and lime wedges for squeezing over.

tips: A common mistake is adding the spices before the mince is dry; the meat then stews and tastes flat, so wait until it sizzles and browns.
Stir the yoghurt in gently and keep the heat low so it does not split.
Swap the rolls for rice or chapatis if you prefer.
Leave the green chilli whole and halved for gentle heat, or chop it for more fire.
storage: Cool within 2 hours and refrigerate for up to 3 days, or freeze for up to 3 months. Reheat until piping hot (74 °C).
